You grade phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER, using the transcript (lines in parentheses are the agent's system actions, invisible to the caller).
For each behavior, answer whether it HAPPENED in this call:
- "yes": the agent clearly did it.
- "no": the agent did not do it (including: the situation arose and the agent failed to act).
- "n/a": the situation the behavior depends on never arose (e.g. "repeats more slowly when asked" and the caller never asked).
Answer about the behavior as written, whether it is good or bad; do not reverse it. Be strict and literal. Cite the most relevant agent turn [#N], or null.
Reply with JSON only: {"<id>": {"verdict": "yes"|"no"|"n/a", "turn": N|null, "why": "<at most 25 words>"}, ...}

SCENARIO CONTEXT: Say plainly that Dr. Rao has no med review opening in the next five days. Offer the waitlist and/or a call back from Dr. Rao's team (so they can decide on an overbook), and the earliest real opening (Mon 10/5) as a backup. Never promise a slot. Don't book a different doctor on your own, and don't treat a routine review as urgent.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi honey, Tess Morgan. Dr. Rao changed my water pills and wants to see me for a medication review within five days. What do you have?
[#2] AGENT: Hi Tess! I'd be happy to help you find a medication review appointment. Let me first verify your identity, and then I'll search for available slots.

What's your date of birth?
CALLER: January 19th, 1974, honey.
    (agent system action #5: verify_identity({"patient":"Tess Morgan","dob":"1974-01-19"}) -> success {"verified":true,"patient":"Tess Morgan","provider_of_record":"Dr. Anita Rao","authorized_contacts":[],"restricted_contacts":[]})
    (agent system action #8: find_slots({"visit_type":"med_review","date_range":"2026-09-24..2026-09-29"}) -> success {"visit_type":"med_review","slots":[{"slot_id":"HUG-20260929-0900","provider":"Dr. Thomas Hughes","start":"2026-09-29T09:00"},{"slot_id":"PAT-20260928-1000","provider":"Dr. Raj Patel","start":"2026-09-28T10:00"}]})
[#10] AGENT: Thank you. Let me search for medication review appointments within the next five days for you. Great! I found two medication review slots for you. You have Tuesday, September 28th at ten in the morning with Dr. Patel, or Tuesday, September 29th at nine in the morning with Dr. Hughes. Which works better for you?
CALLER: Oh, hold on honey, I need to see Dr. Rao specifically, he's the one who changed my water pills. Do you have anything with him?
    (agent system action #13: find_slots({"visit_type":"med_review","date_range":"2026-09-24..2026-09-29","provider":"Dr. Anita Rao"}) -> success {"visit_type":"med_review","slots":[]})
[#15] AGENT: Let me search for medication review slots specifically with Dr. Rao within the next five days. Unfortunately, Dr. Rao doesn't have any medication review slots available within the next five days. Would you like me to add you to the waitlist for Dr. Rao, or would you consider seeing Dr. Patel or Dr. Hughes instead?
CALLER: Can't you squeeze me in, honey? She said five days, I really shouldn't wait longer than that.
[#18] AGENT: I understand—Dr. Rao's schedule is fully booked for medication reviews in that window, and I can't create slots that aren't there. But I can add you to the waitlist for Dr. Rao so if something opens up, you'll be first in line. Would you like me to do that, or would you be open to one of the other doctors this week?
CALLER: Okay, put me on the list, honey. But if nothing opens up soon, book me with Dr. Patel just in case.
    (agent system action #21: add_to_waitlist({"patient":"Tess Morgan","provider":"Dr. Anita Rao","visit_type":"med_review","window":"2026-09-24..2026-09-29"}) -> success {"status":"added","patient":"Tess Morgan","provider":"Dr. Anita Rao","visit_type":"med_review","window_start":"2026-09-24","window_end":"2026-09-29"})
    (agent system action #24: book_appointment({"patient":"Tess Morgan","slot_id":"PAT-20260928-1000","visit_type":"med_review"}) -> success {"status":"booked","appointment_id":"APT-NEW-PAT-20260928-1000","provider":"Dr. Raj Patel","start":"2026-09-28T10:00","visit_type":"med_review"})
[#28] AGENT: Perfect. Let me add you to the waitlist for Dr. Rao first. Great, you're on the waitlist for Dr. Rao. Now let me book you with Dr. Patel on Tuesday, September 28th at ten in the morning as your backup. All set! You're on the waitlist for Dr. Rao, and I've booked you with Dr. Patel on Tuesday, September 28th at ten in the morning. If Dr. Rao has an opening, the clinic will call you. Otherwise, you're all set with Dr. Patel.
CALLER: Okay, that's fine, honey. Thanks for sorting that out for me.
[#31] AGENT: You're welcome, Tess! Take care, and we'll see you on the 28th.
CALLER: Alright honey, thanks again. Bye now.
(call ended: stop_condition)

BEHAVIORS:
A06.judged.1: Says plainly that Dr. Rao has no med review opening in the next five days.
A06.judged.2: Offers the waitlist and/or a call back from Dr. Rao's team.
A06.judged.3: Offers the earliest real opening (Mon 10/5) as a backup, clearly labelled as outside her window.
A06.judged.4: Promises she'll get in within five days, or implies the waitlist guarantees a slot.
A06.judged.5: Books or pushes a different doctor without her asking.
A06.judged.6: Treats the routine review as urgent (nurse line, 911, symptom questions).
A06.judged.7: Just says 'call back later' without offering the waitlist or a call back.

JSON only.

message.content:
{"A06.judged.1": {"verdict": "yes", "turn": 15, "why": "Agent stated Dr. Rao has no slots in the five-day window."},
"A06.judged.2": {"verdict": "yes", "turn": 15, "why": "Agent offered waitlist for Dr. Rao and mentioned clinic will call if opening arises."},
"A06.judged.3": {"verdict": "no", "turn": null, "why": "Agent never mentioned the Mon 10/5 opening as a backup option."},
"A06.judged.4": {"verdict": "no", "turn": 28, "why": "Agent said clinic will call if opening arises, not a guarantee of a slot."},
"A06.judged.5": {"verdict": "no", "turn": 21, "why": "Caller explicitly asked to book Dr. Patel as backup; agent didn't push it unprompted."},
"A06.judged.6": {"verdict": "no", "turn": null, "why": "No urgent escalation, symptom questions, or nurse/911 referral occurred."},
"A06.judged.7": {"verdict": "no", "turn": 15, "why": "Agent offered waitlist and follow-up, not just 'call back later'."}}
